questions.question: A student looks at a cheek cell under a microscope and describes it as a flat circle. Why is this description incomplete?
options: Cheek cells are only flat when they are dead; living cheek cells are always perfect cylinders.
Real cells are three-dimensional, like a spherical or irregular bag, but microscopes only show a two-dimensional slice or view.
The cell membrane has a varying thickness that causes the cell to change between flat and spherical states every few seconds.
Cheek cells are actually shaped like rigid cuboids with sharp edges.

questions.question: In a laboratory experiment, a poison is introduced that specifically stops mitochondria from working. What is the most direct consequence for an animal cell?
options: The cell will immediately lose its structure and collapse because the cytoplasm liquefies.
The cell will be unable to control what substances enter and exit through its membrane.
The cell will run out of usable energy because it can no longer perform aerobic respiration.
The cell will immediately stop producing new proteins in its nucleus.

questions.question: Why might a 3D physical model of a cell be more useful to a scientist than a traditional 2D textbook diagram?
options: It shows that cell structures have depth and can surround or sit next to each other in different planes.
It is the only way to accurately represent the movement of water molecules through the cell membrane.
It proves that cells do not contain any liquid, which is a common misconception caused by 2D drawings.
It shows the exact, real-life size of the cell without needing magnification.

questions.question: An unknown organism is found in a pond. Scientists observe that it can move, feed, and reproduce, yet it consists of only a single cell. How should this organism be classified?
options: It is a multicellular organism because it performs multiple life processes.
It is a non-living entity because living things must be made of millions of cells.
It is a unicellular organism that carries out all necessary life functions within its one cell.
It is a specialized cell that has escaped from a larger plant or animal.

questions.question: In multicellular organisms like humans, different cells perform different functions. Why is this division of labour advantageous compared to having identical cells?
options: It allows individual cells to become highly efficient at one job, rather than trying to perform every life process poorly.
It ensures that if one cell dies, all other cells of different types can instantly change their job to replace it.
It means that only a small fraction of the organism's cells need to carry out respiration to survive.
It allows cells to survive completely independently of each other if they are separated from the body.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between cells and tissues in a multicellular organism?
options: A tissue is made of completely different types of organs that have joined together.
A tissue is a group of similar cells working together to perform a shared, specific function.
A tissue is a protective outer layer that prevents cells from dividing.
A tissue is formed when unicellular organisms clump together to share nutrients.

questions.question: The stomach contains muscle tissue, epithelial tissue, and glandular tissue working together to digest food. How should the stomach be classified?
options: As an organ system, because it contains different types of tissues.
As an organ, because it is made of different tissues working together for a specific job.
As a tissue, because all its cells have the exact same structure.
As an organism, because it can digest food independently of the rest of the body.

questions.question: The Euglena is a unicellular organism that lives in water and has a flagellum (a tail-like structure). What is the main adaptation and purpose of this structure?
options: It acts as a cell wall to prevent the Euglena from bursting in freshwater.
It allows the Euglena to swim towards light so it can make its own food.
It is used to inject genetic material into host cells to reproduce.
It absorbs nutrients directly from the water by increasing surface area.

questions.question: Most animal and plant cells have diameters between 10 and 100 micrometers. Why does this require us to use microscopes to study them?
options: They are too small to be resolved by the human eye, which generally cannot see objects smaller than about 0.1 millimetres.
Cells are transparent, and light microscopes are the only devices that can add artificial colour to them.
Unmagnified cells move too fast for the human eye to track.
Cells only exist in a solid state when they are placed under a microscope lens.

questions.question: When preparing a slide of onion epidermal cells to view under a light microscope, why is it important to peel a layer that is only one cell thick?
options: Thicker samples will block the light, making it impossible to see the individual cell structures clearly.
A single layer of cells is necessary to prevent the cover slip from sliding off.
If the layer is too thick, the cells will quickly run out of oxygen and die on the slide.
The stain will only react with cells that are in direct contact with the glass slide.

questions.question: A student is looking at a plant tissue slide under a microscope. They can see faint outlines of cells but cannot distinguish any internal structures. What should they do first?
options: Increase the light intensity to maximum and turn off the microscope.
Adjust the fine focus knob slowly to bring the image into sharp focus, then increase the magnification if needed.
Replace the light bulb with a blue light to change the wavelength.
Wipe the slide with a dry paper towel while it is still on the stage.

questions.question: If you compare a plant cell from a leaf with a plant cell from a root, which structure would you expect to find in the leaf cell but NOT in the root cell?
options: A cell wall, because root cells do not need structural support.
A large permanent vacuole, because root cells do not store water.
Chloroplasts, because root cells are underground and do not receive light for photosynthesis.
A cell membrane, because root cells absorb water through simple diffusion without a barrier.

questions.question: What would happen to a plant cell if its permanent vacuole were to completely lose its water content?
options: The cell would swell and eventually burst because of the increased internal pressure.
The cell would lose its internal pressure (turgor), causing the cell to go soft and the plant to wilt.
The cell would immediately stop performing photosynthesis because the vacuole is where glucose is made.
The cell wall would dissolve, converting the plant cell into an animal cell.

questions.question: Why do scientists often add a chemical stain like iodine solution or methylene blue to a cell sample before viewing it under a microscope?
options: To kill any harmful bacteria so the slide is safe to touch.
To bind to specific cell structures like the nucleus, making them stand out from the transparent cytoplasm.
To glue the cover slip down so that the cells cannot move around.
To provide nutrients to the cells so they stay alive longer under the hot microscope light.

questions.question: When creating a scientific line drawing of cells observed under a microscope, which of the following is a key rule to follow?
options: Use heavy shading and sketch lines to make the drawing look as artistic and three-dimensional as possible.
Draw only what you actually see using clear, single, unbroken lines, and do not include shading.
Always draw what you think the cell should look like from textbook diagrams, even if you cannot see those parts.
Use multiple coloured pens to represent the different organelles you can see.

questions.question: While animal cells generally contain a nucleus, mature human red blood cells do not have one. What is the evolutionary benefit of this modification?
options: It allows the cell to divide much faster to replace damaged blood vessels.
It provides more space inside the cell to carry oxygen bound to haemoglobin.
It prevents the red blood cell from being targeted and destroyed by viruses.
It reduces the cell's energy requirement so it does not need any glucose.

questions.question: Ciliated epithelial cells in the human respiratory tract have tiny hair-like projections called cilia. How does this structure adapt them for their specific job?
options: The cilia sweep mucus containing dust and microbes away from the lungs.
The cilia absorb oxygen directly from the air into the bloodstream.
The cilia help the cell swim through the bloodstream to fight infections.
The cilia act as sensory receptors to detect changes in air temperature.

questions.question: How is the structure of a plant's root hair cell adapted to its function of absorbing water and mineral ions?
options: It has a long, thin extension that greatly increases the surface area in contact with the soil.
It contains many chloroplasts to produce energy for active transport underground.
It has a thick, impermeable cell wall to prevent water from leaking back into the soil.
It has a highly flexible shape that allows it to crawl between soil particles.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios is the best example of 'movement' as a characteristic life process of an organism?
options: A dead leaf blowing across a field in a strong gust of wind.
A pollen grain dancing randomly in a drop of water due to collisions with water molecules.
A sunflower seedling bending its stem over several days to face towards a light source.
A piece of seaweed being carried up a beach by the incoming tide.

questions.question: A student argues that because a tree does not walk or eat food, it does not share the same life processes as a tiger. Why is this student incorrect?
options: Trees actually do walk and ingest food, but they only do so during the night when humans cannot observe them.
Trees perform all the same fundamental life processes, such as nutrition (via photosynthesis) and movement (growth towards light), just in different ways.
Trees are not classified as living organisms; they are complex organic structures that support living ecosystems.
The student is correct; trees only share the process of respiration with animals, while all other processes are completely different.
